contexts.text: To trade, that is, to buy and sell, = to procure the Knowledges of good and truth, and, through them, good itself.
Sell thy birth-right ()... To sell = to claim for itself.
He hath sold us () = that he had alienated them.
Go ye rather to them that sell () = the good of merit: those who boast of it are they that sell. Compare. DSS 17:2.
By their selling the Lord, the like was represented...

Let us sell him to the Ishmaelites () = that those in simple good acknowledge Him; for to sell = to alienate from one's self, thus to be received by others; and, when predicated of truth, it = to be acknowledged. AC 4758. AC 4788.
It may be supposed that as Joseph was sold to the Ishmaelites, he was sold by these into Egypt, and not by the Midianites; but... Divine truth cannot be sold by those who are in good...
Joseph sold to Egypt () = appropriation. To sell = to appropriate to anyone; for that which is sold becomes his who buys it. AC 5418.
To sell = to alienate the things of faith and charity. Explained, Illustrated.

In the Spiritual World, there is no buying and selling such as there is on earth; but the appropriation of good and truth signified by buying, and the alienation of them signified by selling. By selling is also signified the communication of the Knowledges of good and truth. Explained.

The Egyptians sold everyone his field () = the renunciation and subjection of all things which are of service to the Church. To sell = to alienate so that it is no longer his; thus to renounce and subject. AC 6151.
To sell a man of the sons of Israel () = to alienate the truths and goods of faith, and also to make them serve...
When a man shall sell his daughter for a maidservant () = the affection of truth from natural delight. Explained.
To sell = to alienate.
He that stealeth a man and selleth him () = the application of the truth of faith to evil, and alienation.
They shall sell the living ox () = that the affection of the one which had injured... shall be alienated. AC 9101.
He shall be sold for his theft () = the alienation of the good and truth taken away, of which nothing remains. Explained.
That he should sell all things which he had () = that he should remove his heart from riches. ( = to alienate all things which are of our Own love. AE 840:end.)
To buy and sell = to procure for themselves Knowledges, and to teach them, in like manner as to trade, etc. Illustrated. AE 840.
(The Africans) sell such. SE 6095:end.
To sell the sons of Judah... () = to falsify the goods...
To sell nations () = to alienate goods; and to sell families by sorceries = to alienate truths.
To sell () = to pervert.
To go to them that sell, and buy = to those who teach, and learn or procure for themselves...
They that sold and bought () = those who make a profit for themselves from holy things.
To sell, and to be sold, also = to alienate truths, and to be alienated from them, and to accept falsities instead of them, and be captivated by them. Illustrated.
Those who have been alienated through falsities are called sold.
He went and sold all that he had, and bought that pearl () = that he rejected proprium, in order that he might receive life from the Lord.
